Biennial advice and stock-specific choices

Source: vignettes/stock-choices.Rmd
stock-choices.Rmd

The dlsrules helpers have few defaults on purpose: every choice that changes the advice or the history tables is an argument, set in the stock’s config.R. This vignette lists those choices, with what the MFRI category 3 stocks chose, and shows the biennial advice.

library(dlsrules)

The choices of the MFRI stocks

As set in the stocks’ config.R on their dls-harmonise branches (October 2026):

Stock Rule Index Catch lengths (gears) Iloss F proxy series from SSB interval Advice years
04-whg chr smb_b40 BMT, LLN, DSE, NPT, GIL "min" (HR instead) normal 1
13-cas rfb smb_total BMT, LLN "min" 2007 log-normal 2
14-mon rfb smb_b40 BMT, NPT, DSE, GIL, LLN "mean" 1985–1999 all log-normal 2
24-lem rfb smb_harv BMT, DSE, NPT; under 100 cm "min" all log-normal 2
25-wit rfb smb_harv BMT, DSE, NPT "min" all log-normal 2
26-meg rfb smb_harv BMT, DSE, NPT; survey lengths in years without catch samples "min" 1985 log-normal 2
27-dab rfb smb_harv BMT, DSE, NPT "min" all log-normal 2
60-norway-redfish rfb smb_total BMT from 1997 "second_min" all log-normal 2

The F proxy series ends the year before the assessment year in every stock.

Which rule

K decides: rfb for K < 0.32 (rfb_rule() stops otherwise), chr for 0.32 ≤ K < 0.45, and above that neither (short-lived stocks). The multiplier follows K:

sapply(c(0.06, 0.147, 0.3), multiplier_lookup)
#> [1] 0.95 0.95 0.90

Iloss

ICES (2025) defines Iloss as the lowest observed index value, which is method = "min". Two stocks keep the choice of their old assessment, by decision of the stock coordinator: 14-mon uses the mean of 1985–1999, and 60-norway-redfish the second lowest value. The method changes Itrigger, and with it the biomass safeguard:

set.seed(2)
index <- data.frame(
  year = 1985:2025,
  index = round(2000 * exp(cumsum(c(0, rnorm(40, 0, 0.12)))))
)
index$index[41] <- round(0.8 * min(index$index[1:40]) * 1.4)
sapply(
  list(
    min = calc_iloss(index, "min"),
    second_min = calc_iloss(index, "second_min"),
    mean = calc_iloss(index, "mean", years = 1985:1999),
    fixed = calc_iloss(index, "fixed", value = 1500)
  ),
  function(x) x$I_loss
)
#>        min second_min       mean      fixed 
#>   1796.000   1836.000   2285.733   1500.000

Here the last index value is below Itrigger with the lowest value as Iloss, so the biomass safeguard is below 1, and the stability clause is not applied:

z <- 0.12 + 0.05 * sin(seq_along(1990:2024) / 4)
ldist <- expand.grid(length = 20:70, year = 1990:2024)
ldist$n <- round(
  2000 * plogis((ldist$length - 32) / 1.5) *
    exp(-z[ldist$year - 1989] * (ldist$length - 32) / 1.2 * (ldist$length > 32))
)
ldist <- ldist[, c("year", "length", "n")]

advice_by_method <- function(method, ...) {
  rp <- ref_points_iloss(list(K = 0.147, Linf = 62.1, Lc = 33), index,
                         method = method, ...)
  p <- rfb_advice(index, ldist, rp, prev_tac = 1659, assessment_year = 2025)
  setNames(p$value, p$component)[
    c("Iloss", "biomass_safeguard", "stability_clause_applied", "catch_advice")
  ]
}
rbind(
  min = advice_by_method("min"),
  second_min = advice_by_method("second_min"),
  mean = advice_by_method("mean", years = 1985:1999)
)
#>            Iloss biomass_safeguard stability_clause_applied catch_advice
#> min         1796         0.8001909                        0     840.9711
#> second_min  1836         0.7827575                        0     822.6493
#> mean        2286         0.6287448                        0     660.7875

The length data of the rule

catch_ldist() takes the gears and the first year. To make the rule’s distribution from a table collected by gear, use rule_ldist():

ld_gear <- data.frame(
  year = rep(2023:2024, each = 4),
  mfdb_gear_code = rep(c("BMT", "DSE", "GIL", "BMT"), 2),
  length = c(30, 40, 50, 236, 31, 41, 51, 45),
  n = c(10, 5, 2, 1, 8, 6, 4, 2)
)
# 24-lem: gears of the rule, and lengths under 100 cm, which drops a
# mis-entered 236 cm fish
rule_ldist(ld_gear, gears = c("BMT", "DSE", "NPT"), max_length = 100)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 3
#>    year length     n
#>   <int>  <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1  2023     30    10
#> 2  2023     40     5
#> 3  2024     31     8
#> 4  2024     41     6
#> 5  2024     45     2
# 26-meg: add survey lengths in a year without catch samples of the gears
survey_ld <- data.frame(year = 2025, length = c(44, 48), n = c(3, 1))
rule_ldist(ld_gear, gears = c("BMT", "DSE", "NPT"), max_length = 100,
           extra = survey_ld)
#> # A tibble: 7 × 3
#>    year length     n
#>   <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1  2023     30    10
#> 2  2023     40     5
#> 3  2024     31     8
#> 4  2024     41     6
#> 5  2024     45     2
#> 6  2025     44     3
#> 7  2025     48     1

lag (default 1) is the number of years between the assessment year and the year of the length data. Use 0 only when the lengths come from a survey of the assessment year.

Lc and Linf

They are fixed in config.R until a benchmark: Lc at 50% of the modal abundance (or a fixed value, 04-whg), Linf from growth or from the catch (25-wit and 27-dab: 0.9 × the largest length; 04-whg: linf_from_catch(p = 0.998)). Re-estimating them each year changes LF=M, the advice and the whole F proxy series.

Intervals in the assessment summary

assessment_summary(ssb_ci, rec_ci): log-normal for all stocks but 04-whg’s SSB index (normal, as its old code). See vignette("history-tables").

Biennial advice

Most of the rfb stocks give advice every second year, for two fishing years. Three things follow.

The assessment year is the year of the advice, not the current year. In the years between, the previous advice stands, and the pipeline must reproduce it. 25-wit, 13-cas, 14-mon and 27-dab take the latest odd year:

assessment_year_of <- function(today) {
  2025L + 2L * ((as.integer(format(today, "%Y")) - 2025L) %/% 2L)
}
assessment_year_of(as.Date(c("2025-06-01", "2026-10-09", "2027-03-01")))
#> [1] 2025 2025 2027

24-lem, 26-meg and 60-norway-redfish set assessment_year <- 2025 by hand. data_year (the last year with complete catches) is assessment_year - 1; don’t use assessment_year for it.

The previous advice (prev_tac) is the advice for the fishing year that starts the year before the assessment year, which for a biennial advice is the second year of the previous advice:

prev_tac = readr::read_csv(historical_advice_file, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::filter(assessment_year == .env$assessment_year - 1) |>
  dplyr::pull(advice)

This needs a row for that year in data/advice_hist.csv, which the previous assessment wrote with n_years = 2.

The advice history gets two rows:

prognosis <- rfb_advice(
  index, ldist,
  ref_points_iloss(list(K = 0.147, Linf = 62.1, Lc = 33), index, "min"),
  prev_tac = 1659, assessment_year = 2025
)
advice_hist_rows(prognosis, assessment_year = 2025, n_years = 2)
#>   assessment_year advice_period advice advice_basis.en advice_basis.is
#> 1            2025     2025/2026    841 Domestic advice Innlend ráðgjöf
#> 2            2026     2026/2027    841 Domestic advice Innlend ráðgjöf

Pitfalls

  • Defaults of old calls: when porting, check every argument the old code left out. The choices above reproduce each stock’s published advice; harmonising them is a decision for the stock coordinator, not a code change.
  • The year convention: a history file that contains a newer assessment year than assessment_year makes the advice recompute the wrong year.
  • Survey index by length range: the length ranges of the indices (smb_harv: over 30 cm in 25-wit) have exclusive ends, as tidypax had, and the station strata come from the fixed station list (pax::pax_si_strata_stations()). Both change the index and so the advice.

AI use

This vignette was drafted with Claude (Anthropic) in October 2026 and has not yet been checked by a person (MFRI policy on the use of AI). The data are simulated.
